review.verdict: J2 delivered a done-when-complete single-file site in 2 cycles for 68 of 100 budget with no redirects, refusals or invalid moves, but the run barely tested negotiation, conflict or pause paths and the overflow fix was never measured.

identity.note: Wrote a valid charter (11 checkable items) and gave an honest done verdict with two caveats [24]. It bundled three decisions into one CEO ask [2], though the role file says one bounded decision. It did not overreach otherwise.

ceo.note: Chose one option per question, gave a one-sentence reason each, and stated that the brief was silent [3]. Picks were not the first-shown option (shown positions 1, 2, 2) and only 1 of 3 matched Identity's first option. Three decisions is too few to call bias.

adaptation.note: Smallest workable split (W1 base, W2 order form) with a budget and reserve [6]. The fix proposal admitted the cause was unverified [16]. Evidence of the full proposal fields is not visible in the chat.

priority.note: Granted with cost breakdown, reserve and retry limit [7][17]. Stayed out of scheduling. It never countered or refused, so its bargaining role is untested.

coordination.note: Stated the scheduling rule and the lock on site.html each time, with nothing held [9][11][19]. In [19] it added instructions (find the element first, CSS only, do not touch the script), which edges into changing workflow steps.

audit.note: Cited the failed criterion, did not guess the cause, routed to Adaptation for a defect [15] and to Identity for done [23]. It flagged that the wa.me path was read but not run, and that the fix is verified only by result.

builder.note: Stayed in scope on all three workflows [10][12][20]. In W-3 it said plainly that it had no browser and the cause was a guess [20]. The fix worked, but by luck or inference, not measurement.

went_well: Clean run: 16 AI calls, 5 minutes, 3 of 3 workflows done, 0 validator refusals, 0 role refusals, 0 redirects.
The code-run 360px check caught a 61px overflow that Builder had no way to see [14], and the re-check confirmed 0px after the fix [22]. The audit, fix, re-audit loop worked.
Every agent reported its limits: unmeasured cause [20], unrun wa.me path [23], placeholders left open [24].
Placeholders were handled by rule: 8 open inputs listed, none blocked done, and no invented facts are visible in the chat.
problems: The overflow fix was a guess ('fixed-width price spans') [20]. If a similar defect recurs, the Builder cannot find it without tooling.
The wa.me submit path was never executed [23]. Done-when item 5 passed on code reading only.

Negotiation paths were not exercised: 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 conflicts, 0 pauses. Estimates equaled charges exactly (25/25, 35/35, 8/8), so the rate card did Priority's job and cost discipline was not tested.

The done-when list passes with every menu item, price, area, address and hour as a placeholder, so 'done' is a template, not a usable site. That bar is set by the charter, not a J2 fault, but it limits what this result proves.
Identity's ASK_CEO bundled three questions, against the role format. Coordination added scope constraints in [19].
learnings: Keep the code-run phone and desktop overflow check. It was the only thing that found the defect [14][22].
Change: make the mechanical check name the offending element, or give Builder a headless browser. Audit said the cause was untraceable [15] and Builder guessed [20].
Change: add a mechanical wa.me test that runs the submit handler with a dummy number and checks the URL. It closes the gap in [23] at low cost.
Test next: rerun with a tight budget (for example 40) so Priority must counter and the Adaptation/Priority and CEO-conflict paths run. This run gives no evidence on them.
Test next: a brief where done-when needs Requester-only facts with no placeholder allowance, to exercise the pause rule (0 pauses here).
Test next: remove the rate card or let Adaptation estimate freely, so estimate-vs-charged is a real signal.

Role files: amend Identity to allow bundled charter-setting questions in the first ASK, since the bundle worked [3]. Keep one decision per ASK after that. Team, CEO and Builder files are still placeholders.
Evidence is thin: one brief, one run, three CEO decisions. Treat all of the above as hypotheses, not findings.
